So an obround from two of them has concave ends (knife-edge tips). The ops click() moves the pointer straight from the start to the end; sketch_mode.rs pointer_move wraps the π step to −π (center_arc_sweep). Any agent or script asking for a 180° arc silently gets the opposite one. Fix: the op sweeps counter-clockwise as documented, whatever the step (e.g. pointer moves along the arc); an e2e test with a half-turn.

  (`renderer::share_adapter`), no second instance. Fixed: 0 crashes in 42 starts under gdb (x172, vibex7; 4 in 17 before).

  Mac GPU (qa 02:2x, v0.4.65, plate + scissor, frame log qa-scratch/w7/macnav): Shift+5, Shift+7, Shift+1, F each present 34–35
  frames over ~500 ms, the first 3–19 ms after the key; the cube's ArrowRight 20 frames. Ours animates there, as live does.

- [x] P2 **APP-SIGTERM-IGNORED-MAC (dx)**: on the Mac, `timeout 170` (SIGTERM) quits the app on the plate but not on scissor or
  infento (both regenerate through the kernel): the app stays idle in its run loop with SIGTERM neither blocked nor pending, and a
  second `kill -TERM` does nothing; only SIGKILL ends it. Something installs a SIGTERM handler that doesn't quit. Sample:
  mac:~/noshape-host/qa/w7/scissor-hang.sample.txt. Fixed (dx 11-22, "a recovered fault no longer makes the Mac
  app ignore SIGTERM"): no handler; macOS's sigprocmask sets every thread's mask, and the crash guard's siglongjmp (and
  std::terminate's abort) restored a GCD-made thread's mask (all but fault signals blocked) with it after a recovered OCCT
  fault (infento: a fillet's Geom2dAdaptor fault), so the whole app blocked SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGCHLD. T1 test
  kernel_core::a_recovered_fault_leaves_the_process_ending_on_sigterm (failed on the Mac before).

## asm, 2026-11-19
- [ ] **P2 HOLE-THROUGH-ROUND-POLE [bool]** (asm 20:38, isaac-ball Fastened 43): a Ø6 REMOVE extrude coaxial with an
  R4 corner round, whose axis passes through the corner ball's pole (the ball touching the bottom face at the axis,
  that face's corner vertex), isn't cut: noshape's Boolean declines ("a non-manifold result") and OCCT's returns
  non-manifold ("Boolean operation would result in non-manifold body."); live cuts it. Minimal repro (current CLI):
  vibex8 ~/agents/asm-keep/t-mini-false.sh: an 11 mm 40 × 40 plate, R4 on the corner's vertical edge and its two
  bottom edges, a Ø6 circle at (4, 4) on Top extruded 25 mm Remove (the same circle at (20, 20) cuts 311 mm³). In
  isaac studio 00f1d4 its Extrude 38 ("Selected tools and targets do not intersect"; live removes 303.7 mm³), so the
  hole edge Fastened 43 mates to is missing (isaac 98/129 mates).
- [x] verified (qa 11-20: main CI 44647614148 on 5b62f6ca8, Linux: assembly-ui's 105 tests, then its doc-tests, no SIGSEGV) (asm d671313d) **P1 ASM-UI-SIGSEGV-AT-EXIT [asm]** (lead 17:2x, main CI 44554083714 on eb3b06a88, Linux, first seen):
  `-p noshape-assembly-ui --lib` passed all 97, then the test process died with SIGSEGV at exit. Cause read from the code:
  each headless `Gpu` spawns a detached "noshape-render" thread that compiles its pipelines (lavapipe / LLVM) before it
  reads its channel, and the GPU feel tests make two per test, so the last tests' threads could still be compiling while
  exit() ran Mesa's and LLVM's destructors. Fix: `RenderWorker` joins its thread on drop and skips a compile not yet
  started (test offscreen::a_dropped_render_worker_has_ended_its_thread fails without it). Not reproduced off CI: 15
  runs of the unfixed binary on vibe2 (lavapipe) all exited 0. Reopen if it comes back on CI.

  behind a runtime CPU check: green opened tests/perf/release-fillet-hang.noshape 1.5x faster than v0.4.32 only because
  its TKMesh (and ten other OCCT libraries) had been built for x86-64-v3 by the vibe hosts' GCC 15 default (11-06, all
  rebuilt at baseline). Users with AVX2 CPUs (most) should get that speed: a second TKMesh compiled with -march=x86-64-v3
  and `-ffp-contract=off` (FMA contraction changed learning-center-michael's Fillet 2 when it reached
  math_DirectPolynomialRoots; keep FMA out of anything whose results it could change), its symbols renamed apart and the
  meshing entry points dispatched on `__builtin_cpu_supports("avx2")` / cpuid (Linux and Windows x86-64; arm64 has NEON
  by default). Results identical on both paths: a T1 meshing the perf fixtures and qa's document both ways, comparing
  nodes and triangles exactly. Measure release-fillet-hang and the corpus on both (release.yml's timing step).
  core 11-06 10:40, measured (vibe5, qa's release-fillet-hang): OCCT all baseline 4.94 s; all x86-64-v3 with FMA
  contraction off 4.83 s (2 %, noise); all v3 with FMA 3.14 s (the 1.5-1.7x). So the speed was FMA's: fused
  multiply-adds round differently, which is what changed learning-center-michael's Fillet 2. Built as asked anyway
  (AVX2 TKMesh + our BRepMesh algorithms, symbols and COMDAT groups renamed apart, a CPU dispatch, a T1 meshing eight
  parts both ways bit-identical: it passes): BRepMesh alone 0.756 -> 0.676 s on the degenerate fuzz body (12 %),
  nothing measurable on the others, because meshing's hot work is curve and surface evaluation through virtual calls
  on the model's own (baseline-built) Geom objects. Not worth a second TKMesh, objcopy renaming and its link risks;
  not landed. The prototype: /root/core-scratch/mesh-avx2 (mesh-avx2.patch, build-tkmesh-avx2.py, mesh_algo.cpp).
  Real meshing speed for users would have to come from FMA in code whose results don't matter (display only), which
  the identical-results rule excludes, or from doing less work (our own mesher taking more of BRepMesh's 10 s of the
  corpus's 16 s of meshing).

  environment but not the MSVC CRT's copy that the kernel's C++ `getenv` reads (taken at start-up); Linux / macOS

  once as its default) the C++ side asks through the bridge; the test uses it. Default (off) unchanged everywhere.
  Same pattern, not failing today (owners note): kernel tests boolean_budget.rs / bool_patterns.rs (NOSHAPE_BOOLEAN_
  MEMORY_MB, NOSHAPE_BOP_PARALLEL, NOSHAPE_KERNEL_PROFILE, NOSHAPE_BOOL_NO_SCALE), band_mesh.rs, rust_mesh.rs.
  (11-02 03:45: the switch is gone with the void walls: live refuses every Shell of a solid with a void (1757), so
  such a Shell now fails at once; the test is `shell::a_solid_with_a_void_doesnt_shell`.)
- [x] verified 7b11ede71 (qa 11-02 00:52, qa-scratch/bin/splitnames.py: a Ø20 × 30 cylinder split by Right then Front into 4 quarters, Chamfer 0.8 mm of one quarter's x = 0 cut face: **v0.4.19 chamfers two parts** (Part 1 and Part 3, both 2331.1635 / 9 faces), **green 4a0fc474 only Part 1** (2331.1635 / 9; the other three 2356.1945 / 5)) P0 SPLIT-PIECE-NAMES (core): a revolved body split by two planes into 3 parts; Chamfer "Face of Split 1" (one
  face picked on one part, 0.8 mm, tangent propagation) chamfered the matching face of all three. Cause: OCCT's
  splitter leaves a cut face shared by the two pieces (one face in both solids), so both pieces' faces got one name and
  the reference resolved on every part carrying it. Fixed: `split_solids(.., apart)` / `name_pieces_apart` name a face
  the pieces share apart per piece (`TopoName::Split` under the dividing feature) for every op whose result becomes
  several bodies (Split, booleans into pieces, new bodies, surface results, rips, ribs, the FS host's bodies); a name
  saved before still finds every piece's face through `descends_from` (old documents regenerate as they did: 150 of
  qa's / qa5's / the profile documents identical before and after: part volumes, face / edge counts, statuses). T1
  `split_names::*` (7, five fail on the previous main): pieces name apart (side by side and stacked), Chamfer /
  Fillet / sketch plane / Shell / mate connector / Draft / Extrude up to face on one piece's face change or take
  that piece only, part pattern / mirror / subtraction in two / repeated splits name apart, the old shared name finds
  both faces.

  **mostly runner hardware.** Hosted runners of one OS land on different CPUs (the timing table now names them,
  a4433e68): in four dry runs Linux's fins-400 took 1.36-2.70 s and macOS's knurl 2.17-4.63 s for the same code. On
  the same CPU (AMD EPYC 7763, 4 cores) Windows is 1.29x Linux on fins-400 (2.83 / 2.20 s), 1.17x on knurl (5.31 /
  4.54) and 0.84x on release-fillet-hang (5.61 / 6.69); a Windows run on an EPYC 9V45 did 2.03 / 3.62 / 3.45.
  **mimalloc as Rust's global allocator on Windows** (branch skasm/mimalloc-win, cfg(windows), app and CLI): against
  the baseline on comparable runs, knurl -7 % (5.70 -> 5.31 / 5.25), fins-400 0 to -7 % (2.83 -> 2.83 / 2.62),
  release-fillet-hang -1 to -3 %: real but small, not the gap. Why: Linux profiles (perf, release CLI) put fins-400
  mostly in OCCT's topology code with ~10 % in malloc / free, which OCCT reaches through the C runtime (NATIVE
  allocator), not Rust's; knurl is our NURBS evaluation (NurbsCurve::at 11 %, derivatives, atan2) with the
  allocator ~3 %. Left on the same hardware, 1.2-1.3x on our Rust-heavy documents: candidates the MSVC CRT's math
  (atan2 / sin / cos: glibc picks FMA versions), OCCT's allocations on the Windows heap (OCCT 8's build-time
  allocator: OPT / TBB / JEMALLOC), thread pool / lock behaviour. Comparing them needs runs pinned to one CPU
  (several dry runs, keep the 7763 pairs) or a Windows box to profile.
  skasm 11-06 11:30, lead's rule (bool's macOS: whole process -9 to -18 %, Rust-only ~-4 %, in the noise): 5

  4.51 s (-0.9 %), release-fillet-hang 3.84 -> 3.83 (-0.3 %, rounds swing +-17 %), fins-400 2.34 -> 2.30 (-1.7 %).

  allocator; allocator work dropped** (no OCCT patch; the experiment branches deleted). Open for the rest of the
  1.2-1.3x on the same CPU (CRT math, threads, MSVC codegen of the C++).

## Core modelling (core)
- [ ] P3 PS-INEXACT-INTERSECTION-EDGES (core / bool; dx 2026-11-14 21:01 UTC, lead's decision) **intersection edges up to
  3e-5 m off their faces; make them exact.** Our models' edges where two faces meet are OCCT's approximated
  intersection curves, off their faces by more than Parasolid's 1e-8 m. A Parasolid / STEP file writes them tolerant
  (SP-curves) and every read fits them again, so reading our own file back moves the volume by 1-2e-6 (the exchange
  suite now allows edge tolerance x area, docs/PARITY-SUITES.md §3). The four cases (exchange suite, vibe6
  ~/tmp/dx/exch-ops-main2.log): cf-sheet-metal-model-plus's Part 3 (STEP 10148.3723, x_t 10148.3648 mm³ for the
  model's 10148.3828; its x_t drifts every round, .3648 -> .3723 -> .3755: its extruded face and the side planes at
  x -10 mm, 7 tolerant edges up to 3.3e-5 m, between B-surfaces and planes / cylinders), cf-wave-spring's Part 1 (x_t
  916.6074 for 916.6061), cf-hose-routing's hoses (x_t 7088.0115 for 7088.0265; the four hose walls). The x_t writer's
  `refit` (exact points through Newton on both faces) can't reach 1e-8 on them: the points are noisy at ~1e-8 at those
  shallow plane / B-surface intersections (tried 11-14, dropped). Done when these parts' edges are within 1e-8 m of
  their faces and the round trips are fixed points.
- [ ] P3 SPLIT-EXACT-EXTRUSION-SECTION (core 2026-11-09 02:41) A Split (opSplitFace) by a plane perpendicular to an
  extruded spline face cuts it along the spline itself in Parasolid (live 2291: c2-hunting-knife's Split 2 edge at
  y = -0.25, a cubic of 4 poles, the sketch spline's own parameter); OCCT's section approximates it (degree 5, 6
  poles, same shape to < 1 µm, another parameter). A guided loft along that edge pairs by the parameter, so the
  knife's Loft 3 runs up to 1.3 mm off live's pairing along its guide (its face still within 4.5 µm, the blade
  4983.62 mm³ in live's band 4982.05-4991.53 with the loft fixes of 11-09). Fix: a plane cutting a linear extrusion
  across its direction imprints the basis curve translated (exact, its own parameter), as a plane cutting a
  revolution through its axis gives the generatrix.

  folder's Set library ▸ "My default tolerances", op `documents_set_library`; `libraries.json` in the config dir; one folder per

  that folder's `.noshape` documents (its subfolders as folders, as the documents page shows them), each document's

  parallel and loaded from a precompiled metallib), and frame 1 ~280-550 ms from the workspace drawn (our first-frame
  pipelines ~45-70 ms, then the GPU's first use). The fix: pipelines shipped compiled for the GPU (Metal binary
  archives harvested per Apple GPU family, or `metal-tt` in the macOS release job), GPUI's and ours. Not a fix: the
  off-screen warm-up frame at device ready (perf 42504449807: +54 ms macOS 26, +622 ms macOS 15, reverted 1b1850a2).

    `Ann::And` intersects the two sides' bits. `EntityType.EDGE` = ANY_EDGE = EDGE | SKETCH_EDGE (params.rs:189), and
    `ALLOWS_AXIS` = LINEAR_EDGE | CIRCULAR_EDGE | SKETCH_EDGE | CYLINDRICAL_FACE | MATE_CONNECTOR (studio.rs:738), so the

    / `.CIRCLE` and `EDGE && ALLOWS_DIRECTION`: the "EDGE && LINE -> linear edges" refinement in the comment never
    yields model edges, because `EDGE` doesn't carry LINEAR_EDGE / CIRCULAR_EDGE (or SOLID_EDGE). The
    `std_edge_filters_match_builtin` test only covers std features that have a built-in twin, so it misses custom code.

- [x] verified (qa 11-20 02:36, main 5b62f6ca8 / green a06ec927: solver::a_screw_relation_keeps_its_turns / a_half_ratio_gear_follows_its_driver_round test(s) on main, not ignored (run by the watcher each commit)) (asm 11-07: turns read from where each solve starts; T1 solver a_screw_relation_keeps_its_turns, a_half_ratio_gear_follows_its_driver_round) P0 ASM-RELATION-TURNS (asm) relations compare wrapped angle changes (`solver.rs` `relation_residual`:
  `wrap_angle(v[0] - base)`, base never updated): a Screw or Rack and pinion travels at most ±½ distance per revolution
  from where it was made (a vise jaw stops), and a Gear with a ratio that isn't whole jumps 180° when its driver
  passes ±180°. The same wrapping caps a Revolute's angle (and its limits) at ±180°. Track turns instead.

  variables (`eval.rs` `prepare_relation`, `EmptyScope`) and silently becomes 1 when that fails: `#ratio` or a typo
  gives a 1:1 relation with no error. Evaluate in the assembly's scope as mate offsets do; an invalid expression is an
  error on the field (dialog and op), not 1.
